correctness.rationale: Reconstructed from the actual RESULT.md. For area-uniform X in a regular n-gon, polar integration gives f(theta)=sec^2(t)/(2n tan(pi/n)) in each side-normal sector. The disk-diameter criterion is X·Y≤0; the indicator Fourier cosine series has coefficient -2(-1)^((ell-1)/2)/(pi ell) for odd ell. Independent angles give squared Fourier coefficients and dihedral symmetry kills harmonics not divisible by n; even n therefore gives exactly 1/2. For odd n, A_{n,j}= [n tan(pi/n)]^-1 int_0^pi sec^2(u/n)cos(ju)du. Two integrations by parts bound the uniform Taylor remainder by O(j^-2 n^-6). Independent SymPy integration verified the two polynomial cosine moments and coefficients A=(-1)^j[2/(j²n²)+(2pi²/j²-16/j⁴)/n⁴+O(j^-2n^-6)]; squaring and summing against 1/j yields O(n^-9). Beta(5)=5pi^5/1536 and beta(7)=61pi^7/184320 give 5pi^4/192 and 7pi^6/720 with asserted mod-four sign. Independent mpmath harmonic quadrature for odd n=5,7,9,11,21,41,81,161 corroborated the asymptotics; finite harmonic truncations DO NOT prove the uniform infinite remainder. The proof, not the source verifier output, supports the infinite assertion.
residual_risks: The numerical Fourier sums used finite harmonic cutoffs and the n=161 ninth-scaled error is contaminated by truncation; they are not used to claim an exact ninth-order coefficient.
The argument proves only the asymptotic for odd n→∞ and even-n equality, not a universal finite-n two-term error constant.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality for the TWO evaluated asymptotic constants with a uniform O(n^-9) remainder. The October 2025 Math Stack Exchange answer already gives the all-n Fourier representation, a parity sign and an O(n^-5)-scale upper estimate; none of those antecedents is novel. Its explicit spectral integral is a serious predecessor and mathematically determines the depth, but its displayed bounds do not give the sharp nonzero coefficient or seventh-order term. Extracting these requires a simultaneous n-inverse expansion uniform across infinitely many harmonics, after which exact Dirichlet beta(5), beta(7) sums give the constants. MSE already gives a fifth-order upper-bound scale, but the positive sharp coefficient (proving the exponent cannot be improved), exactly evaluated seventh-order correction, and uniform n^-9 remainder are motivated quantitative facts not tabulated in the inspected predecessors. They measure a strong cancellation beyond second-order geometric polygonal approximation, enabling precise regular-polygon benchmarks; a broad convex-body extremal theorem is not demanded by the value standard. This is a narrow, explicitly bounded asymptotic evaluation, not a new underlying definition, qualitative parity rule or finite experiment.
residual_risks: The new coefficients arise from the already known Fourier integral by asymptotic expansion, so their research significance is that of a sharp exact quantitative benchmark, not a general theory.
No downstream application or arbitrary-convex-set optimality is proven.
